1.why: Screenshots show a clean sans-serif typeface with ample letter and line spacing across all pages.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case, no italics or all-caps, and consist only of short non-dense sentences.

3.why: Content is in narrow centered cards with clear hierarchy that would reflow readably on mobile, though screenshots themselves are desktop-width.

4.why: Every instruction is a single short sentence in plain language (e.g., 'Choose manual entry and enter this setup secret').

5.why: Pre-filled email/phone act as weak examples, but no example or placeholder is shown for the expected six-digit authenticator code format.

6.why: No screen requires reading any long block of text; all copy is brief labels and one-line instructions.

7.why: The long setup secret is rendered as ordinary selectable text in a box so it can be copied, although no explicit copy button is present.

8.why: No QR code or any alternative to typing the setup secret is offered on the authenticator screens.

9.why: Standard HTML inputs are used (so browser autofill is possible) but there is no visible autocomplete attribute, password-manager hook, or other evidence of support.

10.why: Page headings and the blue primary button stand out clearly on every step, yet no step indicator or progress cue is shown.

11.why: Each screen presents only one primary action button (Verify and continue / Set up authenticator app / Confirm code).

12.why: New screen titles imply the next step and logs record completion, but the main UI never explicitly states what just happened or what comes next.

13.why: After the error the user can simply edit the code and resubmit without penalty; the secret remains visible, though no reveal/hide or re-request controls appear.

14.why: The message 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' neither names the problem (invalid code) nor explains how to fix it.

15.why: No countdown, session timer, or other time limit is displayed on any screen for reading or code entry.
